gates.observation: Each row links a 64x64 image to numeric sensors and actuator factors. Buchholz environments and CITRIS flags identify interventions. A future evaluator could expose opaque environment IDs while withholding R,G,B,pol_1,pol_2.

Official CCRL and multiview splits are random 80/10/10 splits retaining the same environment proportions. CITRIS uses consecutive segments of one process and a uniform factor-recovery evaluation. No public split holds out a physical world or mixing function.

The 60K interventional, 100K temporal and 2K uniform protocols are different tasks and sampling processes, not three scales of one transfer contrast. Sample subsizing would be an evaluator-created scale and would not add worlds.
Row/image pairing and opaque environment IDs permit pair-breaking, intervention-shuffle and consistent channel/permutation controls without exposing semantic variable names.

PCA, ICA and CCA apply to paired views; adaptive linear and autoregressive controls apply only to the temporal protocol; causal controls apply to intervention environments. They do not share one task/input contract, though acquisition, fit, query, state and workload can be charged.

The official multiview experiment groups image and sensor variables using the known causal graph and relies on ground-truth content selection during training. Image, scalar-view and temporal interfaces are method-specific rather than one frozen source-identical learner contract.

All real protocols use one Light Tunnel Mk1 camera configuration and one physical mixing system. Metrics recover the five actuator factors or their graph; train/test partitions do not test transfer to a new physical world or mixing function.
